{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABbxgzEw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhFVHr8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 134, "title": "Replace Sound checkbox with an always-visible mute and volume slider", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator has a binary **Sound** checkbox but no way to adjust playback volume. Users have to change their system volume, and a new volume control must not add a second, redundant sound toggle or a popover that requires an extra click.

The maintainer has selected a compact, **always-visible combined mute + volume slider**: remove the old Sound checkbox and replace it with one cohesive control directly in the existing playback toolbar. Do **not** put the slider behind a speaker icon, menu, details or modal.

Current `main` baseline: `244f72f3c3a0aa47d92eaa4fedf7087fac922e7b`. In [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), the toolbar contains `<label class="sound"><input id="sound" type="checkbox" checked> Sound</label>`. In [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), sound is gated by that checkbox and each `AudioBufferSourceNode` connects directly to `audio.destination`; there is no output gain. [web/style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css) has narrow portrait and short landscape constraints.

## Expected UX

One compact inline audio group, **always visible** alongside **Play/Pause, Reset and Fullscreen**:

```
[Play/Pause] [Reset]  [🔊 mute toggle] [────●──── volume]  [Fullscreen]
```

- [ ] **Remove the old separate Sound checkbox**; keep a single combined volume/mute control, without duplicating its purpose elsewhere.
- [ ] Provide an accessible icon button for **Mute/Unmute** immediately beside a **native range slider**, adjustable from 0% to 100%. These are the two parts of one cohesive control, not two separate sound settings.
- [ ] Keep both controls **always displayed** in the same toolbar position with or without a cartridge, while playing or paused. Do not conditionally replace them with other UI after inserting a ROM.
- [ ] Moving the slider changes the output level **immediately while playing**, without stopping/reloading emulation. 0% is silent and the icon reflects mute; increasing above zero restores audible sound. Mute toggles silence without discarding the last nonzero level; unmuting restores that level. Adjusting the slider above 0 when muted unmutes. Avoid contradictory icon/slider/readout states.
- [ ] Initial default: **100% and unmuted**, matching today's effective volume unless a previously saved user preference exists. Persist the setting across reloads in local browser storage; handle storage denial/corruption gracefully without interrupting audio or gameplay.
- [ ] The master volume is an **emulator/browser preference** shared across the two bundled demo games (潮鳴りの密室 and 夜鳴き鐘) and locally opened ROMs. Switching cartridges, Reset, Play/Pause, and fullscreen should not change the selected volume or mute state.
- [ ] Keep the UI concise and visually subordinate to the emulator screen. Use grouping and spacing rather than explanatory prose, per [README UI/UX](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable**.

## Audio implementation guidance

Use a **single master `GainNode`** in the browser Web Audio output path (conceptually `source → masterGain → audio.destination`), rather than changing Rust DSP output samples or generating fresh gain nodes per source. All scheduled/overlapping audio buffers should pass through the gain stage so a slider/mute change affects **already queued sound** promptly as well as future buffers. Set gain in the range 0–1; never amplify beyond the current 100% baseline. Optionally smooth rapid gain changes to avoid audible clicks while remaining responsive. Preserve the current 32 kHz stereo queueing, bounded lookahead, flushAudio semantics, sound error reporting and AudioContext user-gesture unlock.

When gain is 0 or mute is enabled, playback/video/controller input must continue normally. Audio may remain scheduled but silent. Muting should not be conflated with pausing emulation, and failure to unlock audio must not prevent gameplay; volume or unmute gestures may retry sound activation as allowed by the browser. Update any old `sound.checked` assumptions in JS/tests.

## Responsive/accessibility constraints

- **Desktop:** compact inline audio control in the playback toolbar, not an audio settings panel.
- **Narrow mobile portrait:** visible icon and usable thumb/track beside the playback actions without a long horizontal overflow or crowding the 12 virtual SNES buttons. A sensible wrapping arrangement is allowed if it preserves the screen/control hierarchy.
- **Short-height mobile landscape:** slider is still **always visible and operable**, fitting the central toolbar without clipping, overlapping the central canvas, or displacing the left/right SNES control clusters; adapt track width/spacing or compact toolbar layout instead of hiding the slider.
- Use an accessible mute button name/state and a correctly labeled native range input (e.g. `Volume`, value 0–100, keyboard arrows/home/end). Retain visible focus indication, adequate touch hit areas and understandable muted state for screen-reader users. No tooltips or lengthy text needed for ordinary discovery.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A real browser desktop/portrait/landscape view shows **one always-visible inline mute button plus volume slider**, no old Sound checkbox, and the same basic layout before/after cartridge insertion; include actual implementation screenshots, not concept mockups.
- [ ] Start both bundled demos and a local test ROM; adjust 0%, 25%, 50%, 100% while playing and verify actual output attenuation, not merely slider movement. All active/pending buffer sources run through the master gain; gameplay frame/input progression is unaffected.
- [ ] Verify muted → unmuted restores the previous nonzero volume, dragging above zero unmutes, and the slider's zero-volume icon semantics are correct. Changing volume while paused, switching game, resetting and resuming yields the expected volume.
- [ ] Reload with stored settings and verify persistence. A blocked/unavailable `localStorage` must not crash or block play. Audio-context suspended/error recovery remains usable, and no autoplay-audio permission bypass is introduced.
- [ ] Real Playwright/Chromium behavior checks include keyboard and touchscreen slider adjustment, mute accessibility/labels/focus, phone portrait and short landscape geometry, no horizontal scroll or screen/controller obstruction, intact 12-button touch/gamepad/keyboard support, Pages/CSP/subpath behavior, and no console errors. Test effective gain using a suitable browser instrument or captured output; do not rely only on static DOM assertions.
- [ ] Preserve cartridge selection/autoplay, Reset-to-playing, SRAM save protection, source-built test fixtures, two pinned demo ROM hashes/licenses, published asset allowlist and existing relevant test suites. Run the production Wasm/site build and full applicable browser tests; report mandatory CI checks appropriately and skips honestly.
- [ ] Update concise visible help/README references to the old Sound checkbox without introducing new prose-heavy sections or dependencies.

## Optional validation

Physical iOS Safari / Android Chrome and headphone-listening feedback for rapid gain changes; optional when required automated checks pass.

## Post-merge verification

After merge, inspect the new main Pages deployment and test the actual published app at desktop, portrait and landscape sizes for visible volume control, working mute, smooth live volume adjustment and no page errors. Record deployment run and live-check evidence. This is **after merge**, not a pre-merge gate. On failure, open a separate `task` issue when invoked; no background monitoring is assumed.

- [#122](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/122): unified cartridge selection and autoplay.
- [#128](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/128): cartridge prompt and Reset-to-playing refinement.
